claims.citation: New York Herald, 26 September 1866, p. 6, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The steamship Atlantic, from Southampton, August
10, reached this port yesterday, bringing our files from
London dated on her day of sailing.

claims.citation: New York Herald, 26 September 1866, p. 3, col. 1
claims.verbatim:
The steamship Atlantic, Captain Hoyer, which left
Southampton on the 10th of September, arrived at this
port yesterday afternoon.[cut]
Our European files by the Atlantic are dated on Mon-
day, the 10th of September, two days later than the
papers to hand by the Java, and contain interesting de-
tails of our despatches by the cable to that day.

claims.citation: Hubbard & Winter, North Atlantic Mail Sailings 1840-75 (USPCS, 1988; rev. 2014), p. 292
New York Herald, 26 September 1866, p. 8, col. 3
claims.verbatim:
Steamship Atlantic, Hoyer, Bremen Sept 6, via South-
ampton 10th, at 9 PM, with mdse and 1156[?] passengers, to
Ruger & Bros. Experienced westerly gales the entire pas-
sage. 22d inst, encountered a severe hurricane, lasting 9
hours; 23d, lat 42 18, lon 61 15, saw bark Honduras (Br), with
mainmast gone by the deck, also mizzen topmast and pole
topgallantmast gone; same day, passed a bark rigged steam-
er, bound W; 24th, lat 40 51, lon 69 17, passed steamer Zillah
(Br), bound E.

topmast and foretopgallantmast gone. Same day passed a bark-rigged
